signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Technicals
signals.text: USD/JPY spot trades at 154.85, holding below its daily SMA20 at 157.36, SMA50 at 159.54, and SMA200 at 158.40. Saxo 25d risk reversals print at -1.95, establishing an acute put skew that reflects substantial institutional demand for downside protection. That options demand contrasts with CFTC positioning, where leveraged funds remain net short JPY by -53,255 contracts despite a massive weekly covering delta of +58,042 contracts. Fed 3.75% vs BoJ 1.0% policy rates yield an OIS carry advantage of +264bp for USD via SOFR 3.62% vs TONA 0.98%, yet options desks are aggressively paying for downside strikes ahead of imminent policy meetings. The positioning shift combined with heavy put skew indicates hedging against a hawkish pivot from Tokyo. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, pressured by extreme downside options skew and short covering. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep. Risk: Fed delivers hawkish forward guidance on 16 Sep that reignites carry demand above 157.36.

signals.title: USD/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: USD outperforms the G10 complex with a 1W average gain of +0.546% across 9 pairs, while SEK anchors the board as the primary laggard at -0.538% across 2 pairs. That generates a 1.084% bilateral spread, clearing the threshold for a pronounced macro divergence theme. The move is underpinned by monetary policy divergence, with Fed 3.75% vs Riksbank 1.75% providing a 200bp nominal carry buffer in favor of the dollar. Fundamental divergence reinforces the price action: Sweden's Economic Surprise Index sits at an extreme -29.2 following persistent macro misses, whereas US data surprises remain neutral at -0.0. USD/SEK spot trades at 9.747, comfortably above its SMA20 at 9.564, SMA50 at 9.591, and SMA200 at 9.349. Trade bias: Long USD/SEK; carry differential and macroeconomic divergence sustain structural upward momentum. Catalyst: FOMC Statement and Interest Rate Decision on 16 Sep. Risk: Riksbank delivers an unexpected hawkish hold on 24 Sep that compresses the bilateral spread below 0.80%.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long
signals.text: AUD/USD spot trades at 0.7131, positioned between its rising SMA50 at 0.7073 and capping SMA20 at 0.7170. CFTC positioning shows leveraged funds net long AUD by +48,379 contracts, residing in the 93rd percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of +1.72. However, weekly flow has stalled, printing a delta of -1,871 contracts while price struggles to push higher. Meanwhile, ATM implied volatility runs at 7.5% against 30-day realized volatility of 5.7%, generating a 1.8-point volatility risk premium that indicates rising demand for balance-sheet protection. A 25-delta risk reversal of -0.78 reveals a moderate put skew, showing that options participants are actively hedging downside rather than funding further topside expansion. Trade bias: Neutral/bearish AUD/USD; stretched spec positioning and protective options pricing leave the pair vulnerable to long unwinds. Catalyst: US Retail Sales print at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Leveraged funds expand net longs with a fresh WoW accumulation above +5,000 contracts.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Macro Flow + Technicals
signals.text: GBP/USD spot trades at 1.3485, hovering just above its SMA50 at 1.3481 and SMA200 at 1.3454, while remaining capped below the declining SMA20 at 1.3501. The cross-asset correlation between GBP/USD and Gold has broken to +0.502 against a 252-day benchmark norm of +0.390, registering a statistically significant deviation of z=+1.59σ. With UK 10Y sovereign yields at 5.39% trading at a +40bp spread over US 10Y Treasuries at 4.99%, the pound is exhibiting sensitivity to broader dollar financing pressures and commodity moves rather than purely domestic drivers. BoE holds at 3.75%. Leveraged funds hold +40,361 net long contracts in the 86th percentile, but momentum is slowing after a weekly reduction of -7,143 contracts. Trade bias: Range GBP/USD; technical moving average support at 1.3481 offsets positioning fatigue. Catalyst: UK CPI release at 06:00 UTC on 16 Sep. Risk: A daily close below the SMA200 at 1.3454 triggers broader institutional long liquidation.
